per_question.question: My app stutters while scrolling. How do I profile it and what general practices help?
per_question.answer: Run the app in profile mode (e.g., `flutter run --profile` or set `flutterMode: "profile"` in launch.json) and open DevTools' Performance view to capture frame timing. You can also record a Timeline with an integration test using `flutter drive --driver=test_driver/perf_driver.dart --target=integration_test/scrolling_test.dart --profile`. In DevTools examine the Flutter frames chart and timeline to spot frames that exceed ~16 ms and identify excessive widget rebuilds. General best‑practice tips are to avoid rebuilding large portions of the UI each frame and to use lazy list widgets such as ListView instead of building a huge list of children directly.

per_question.question: How do I make a web link open a specific screen in my Android app?
per_question.search_query: url_launcher deep link navigate to screen
per_question.answer:
Add an intent‑filter for the VIEW action in your AndroidManifest.xml (see passage 4) so the OS forwards matching http/https URLs to your Flutter app. Then define the deep‑link routes in Flutter (using named routes or the Router as described in passages 1 and 3) so that when the link is opened the app navigates to the desired screen. Example intent‑filter:
```xml
<intent-filter android:autoVerify="true">
    <action android:name="android.intent.action.VIEW" />
    <category android:name="android.intent.category.DEFAULT" />
    <category android:name="android.intent.category.BROWSABLE" />
    <data android:scheme="http" android:host="example.com" />
    <data android:scheme="https" />
</intent-filter>
```
